item.title: Harry Kane makes ultimate gift promise to England and Bayern Munich teammates after emotional Ballon d'Or victory
item.description: FBL-AWARD-BALLON D'OR-2026 - AFP Harry Kane has revealed his plans to treat his Bayern Munich and England colleagues to special gifts following his historic Ballon d'Or triumph in London. The 33-year-old striker enjoyed an incredible 2026, scoring a combined 73 goals for club and country to claim football's most prestigious individual prize. Reaching the pinnacle Kane claimed his maiden Ballon d'Or on Monday night, edging out Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to secure the prestigious accolade. The 33-year-old was honoured in his home city of London, where he delivered a gracious acceptance speech before celebrating at an exclusive Soho nightclub. The recognition follows a breathtaking 2026 campaign for the prolific frontman. Kane registered a staggering 61 goals in just 51 appearances across all competitions for Bayern Munich, while adding another 12 strikes to his international tally with the Three Lions. Watches and rewards Following his crowning moment, Kane confirmed he will share his success with the players who helped him reach the summit. Sporting an ultra-rare Rolex Daytona valued at almost £1 million during the ceremony, the striker admitted his teammates are already expecting extravagant rewards. Speaking to German outlet BILD , Kane outlined his intention to purchase presents for both his club and international colleagues. "Some of the lads have asked for watches or something like that, so I’ll have to come up with something nice for them, both at Bayern and with England," he revealed. "I’ll look into it and make sure I get everyone a nice gift." Arise, Sir Harry? Kane becomes England's sixth Ballon d'Or winner, joining an elite group that includes Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan, and Michael Owen. His unparalleled achievements have sparked discussions in Downing Street regarding a potential knighthood , adding to the MBE he received in 2019. When asked by BILD about the prospect of becoming a knight, Kane embraced the idea while remaining grounded . "I certainly wouldn't say no - I really appreciate it," he said. "If it came to that, it would be incredible and something I'd be incredibly proud of. But I don't want to get too carried away with it right now." Questioned on how "Sir Harry Kane" sounds, the Bayern talisman added: "It sounds good, but it would feel kind of strange if everyone called me Sir. So for now, I'll just stick with Harry." A historic Wembley homecoming Kane is set for a monumental evening on November 12 when England host Croatia in the UEFA Nations League. The captain is expected to parade his Ballon d'Or trophy around Wembley Stadium before kick-off to celebrate the milestone with the home supporters. The fixture carries enormous historical significance for the striker beyond his recent award. item.title: Pirates need to add a veteran starting pitcher
item.description: CLEVELAND, OHIO - JULY 19: Paul Skenes #30 of the Pittsburgh Pirates talks with Braxton Ashcraft #35, Mitch Keller #23 and Jared Jones #17 as he exits the game after the seventh inning against the Cleveland Guardians at Progressive Field on July 19, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Pittsburgh Pirates finished the season with an 82-80 record. The highlight from this year’s team was the offense but the starting pitching was still solid this season. The question is should the Pirates add a veteran free agent arm for next season? The answer in my mind is yes, Pittsburgh absolutely needs to add experience and depth to that starting rotation. This is still a mostly young rotation with Paul Skenes, Jared Jones, Braxton Ashcraft and Bubba Chandler. Mitch Keller is one of the older starters on the club at 30 years old, so this is a very young group. Ashcraft was arguably the top pitcher for the Bucs with a 14-6 record and a 3.65 ERA. While Skenes finished with a 10-11 record 3.82 ERA. While both Keller and Jones missed serious time with injuries. The first veteran pitcher I think the Pirates should look at is Nick Martinez from the Tampa Bay Rays. Martinez helped lead the Rays to the World Series, where he had a 3.10 ERA over 31 starts while earning his first career All-Star nod in 2026. He doesn’t miss a ton of bats, but he averaged an MLB-low 1.30 walks per nine innings this year. The 36-year-old Martinez has a $20 million mutual option for 2027, but he seems likely to decline it and pursue a multi-year deal in free agency this offseason. Another Pitcher is Michael King from the San Diego Padres. King might be a little pricy, but I think he is worth it. The 31-year-old veteran is widely expected to opt out of the three-year, $75 million contract he signed with the Padres last December and re-enter free agency this winter. King struggled to stay healthy in 2025, but he bounced back to post a 3.21 ERA over 32 starts for San Diego this season. There are other names like Freddy Peralta and Tarik Skubal, but those guys will probably be the most expensive starters on the market. The Bucs do have a good starting rotation, but if they add these names or another veteran arm I think it will improve that unit and the team. I understand some of these pitchers might be a little expensive, but this needs to be the offseason where the front office spends money. item.title: Eberl reveals what Oliver Glasner told Bayern about Olise before his move from Crystal Palace
item.description: Eberl reveals what Oliver Glasner told Bayern about Olise before his move from Crystal Palace Michael Olise has established himself as one of the world’s best players since Bayern Munich signed him from Crystal Palace for a reported €53 million in 2024. In an interview with FC Bayern’s club magazine, "51", board member for sport Max Eberl has revealed what convinced the German champions to sign the French winger. “He had a somewhat unsettled career path: he attended several elite football academies in England. But that kind of background doesn’t necessarily have to be a red flag – facing adversity can also help shape a player," Eberl said. “To get to know a footballer, above all, you have to talk to people who have experienced him as either a teammate or an opponent.” Conversations between Bayern sporting director Christoph Freund and his fellow Austrian Oliver Glasner, who was managing Crystal Palace at the time, proved particularly valuable in assessing Olise. “In Michael’s case, we had the advantage that Oliver Glasner was his manager at Crystal Palace at the time – and our sporting director, Christoph Freund, knows Glasner very well,” Eberl said. "When a manager says, ‘Of course, take him, take him,’ it makes you suspicious. But Glasner said, ‘He still has things to learn – and we could really use him.’ That told you he valued Michael highly. "And then there were the conversations with Michael himself: it’s a pleasure to talk football with him.”

item.title: Mourinho’s insistence pays off as 32-year-old fulfils Real Madrid dream after rejecting Barcelona
item.description: Mourinho’s insistence pays off as 32-year-old fulfils Real Madrid dream after rejecting Barcelona Real Madrid signed Bernardo Silva as a free agent back in the summer after his contract with Manchester City expired. Los Blancos secured his signature, beating the likes of Barcelona and Atletico Madrid to it, and expectations were high about what he could add to the midfield. However, it has taken some time for him to settle in, and Madrid’s victory over Barca at the Camp Nou seems like a turning point for the Portuguese midfielder. Bernardo Silva delivered his most convincing performance since arriving in the summer, justifying Jose Mourinho’s determination to bring him to the Bernabeu . According to Diario AS , Silva had long dreamed of representing Madrid, but his initial approach was rejected earlier this year. Mourinho’s return changed everything, with the manager personally pushing for his arrival despite interest from several other European clubs. Mourinho’s intervention changed Bernardo Silva’s future After deciding to leave Manchester City, Silva initially struggled to convince Madrid to pursue his signature. Bernardo Silva is slowly coming into his own at Madrid. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) His agent, Jorge Mendes, subsequently explored alternative destinations, with Barcelona emerging as a serious possibility. However, during a June meeting with Jose Angel Sanchez and Juni Calafat, Mourinho made his intentions clear. “We need a player like Bernardo Silva. We have to secure his signing,” the Portuguese manager insisted. Once Silva learned of Madrid’s interest, he paused other negotiations and prioritised the move. He eventually joined on a free transfer, signing a contract until 2028. Mourinho’s patience rewarded with impressive Clasico display Despite pushing for his signing, Mourinho deliberately managed Silva’s introduction into the team. He wanted the 32-year-old midfielder to regain his physical sharpness before assuming greater responsibilities. That patience paid off against Barcelona, where Silva helped Madrid dictate the tempo and maintain composure against a much more technical midfield. Will Bernardo be a started in the upcoming games? (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) His contribution was particularly important because Madrid had originally identified Rodri as their preferred option to provide control in midfield. While Silva is a different player from his former team-mate, he helped Madrid outplay a midfield featuring Rodri. The Clasico also showed why Silva’s experience matters for Madrid. There is no doubt that he will have an important role to play in the coming weeks . Silva has now taken an important step towards establishing himself as a regular starter, and it remains to be seen how he fares in the upcoming games.

item.title: 'She cold': Tyrese Maxey reacts to meeting Caitlin Clark for the first time ever
item.description: Credit: David Berding/Kevin C. Cox via Getty Images Tyrese Maxey starred for the Philadelphia 76ers in their win over the Indiana Pacers, but he experienced another major highlight off the court. The All-Star guard had the opportunity to meet WNBA superstar Caitlin Clark for the first time at the Gainbridge Fieldhouse, which is her home arena with the Indiana Fever. item.title: FDU basketball to wear jersey patch for special cause this season
item.description: Like a lot of men’s college basketball teams, FDU will debut a patch on its jerseys when the 2026-27 season gets underway next week. Unlike just about everyone else, that patch is not a corporate sponsorship designed to make money. Head coach Jack Castleberry had something else in mind. “What if we found a cause and championed that cause?” he said in pitching his idea to athletics director Jason Young. “It would be an opportunity for us to do some good here.” When the Knights’ take the court at third-ranked Illinois Monday, and for the remainder of their schedule, the upper right corner of their jerseys will read “NDSS” and in smaller letters, “National Down Syndrome Society.” The Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit's mission, “to create a world where individuals with Down syndrome thrive,” is close to Castleberry’s heart. His youngest daughter, 2-year-old Avery, has Down syndrome. And for Castleberry, his wife Kara and their two older daughters (ages 7 and 5), it’s been an eye-opening experience. “I think there’s a lot of misunderstanding out there about what Down syndrome actually is and what the lives are like for those who have Down syndrome,” said Castleberry, who lives in River Edge in Bergen County. “It’s not this terrible thing that I believe most people think it is.” When he and Kara found out Avery would be born with Down syndrome, “it shakes you a little bit” he said. But as he explained, borrowing a line from a book he read on the subject, that was the last bad day. “I can’t speak to everybody’s experience, but my kid is the happiest kid of the three I have,” he said. “She is such a joy. I never thought I would say something like this, but when you’re in front of her, no matter who you are, she sees you. She looks into your soul and there’s a genuine connection. That, I certainly didn’t expect. “You walk into the room with her and your day just brightens up.” Part of Castleberry’s motivation was that he noticed “stuff out there (on social media) about Down syndrome that wasn’t accurate, and to me that was sad,” he said, adding that some of it reached the point where “I felt a little bit threatened for my daughter.” Then he realized he’s got a pretty big forum – FDU’s opener at Illinois will be nationally televised by the Big Ten Network – and the ability to do something about that. “I genuinely proud, and I’m thankful that our administration is not only willing to consider something like this, but adamant about us doing it,” Castleberry said. For the National Down Syndrome Society, this partnership is the first of its kind. “It was really nice to be able to connect with Jack, and that means so much to us because families are at the core of what we do,” said Michelle Sagan, the nonprofit’s director of communications and marketing, who has a sister with Down syndrome. “We hope people see the patch, hear about Down syndrome on the broadcasts, and it really helps people understand our population.” The partnership will extend beyond a patch.

item.title: Giants team up with USA Rugby to tutor NJ high school players
item.description: JERSEY CITY — Even as he cringed at what New York Giants ' management might think, Sisi Mauigoa couldn't help but toss the rugby ball around at Lincoln Park in Jersey City on Oct. 28. After all, the rookie guard played rugby and volleyball growing up in American Samoa before realizing "there was a better future in football." He and NFL teammate Jarrod Gray, a former pro rugby player from Sydney, Australia, showed off their moves for Hudson Catholic players at a clinic on Oct. 28. Three members of the United States women's national rugby team – prop Reece Woods, lock Malia Isaacs and center Kennedy Feasby – also stepped in for tackling drills. Only minimal touching allowed to preserve everyone's health. The women also took their turn throwing and catching the football. Mauioga, a massive 6-foot-6, 335-pound lineman, even awkwardly demonstrated his scoring celebration, which he hopes to do in the end zone someday. "It warmed my heart," Isaacs said of the young players. "I believe in them so much. ... The kids had a spark in them. If they want to go on, they'll be great." Check out our exclusive photo gallery from the USA Rugby and New York Giants clinic, then scroll down for the rest of the story. International doubleheader in NJ The national rugby teams will play an international doubleheader on Oct. 30 at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The women's Eagles are slated to face England in the final match of the WXV Global Series, followed by the men's Eagles' rematch against Australia XV. The American women have won the first four matches in the series , toppling Ireland, Wales and Italy twice. Australia shook off back-to-back losses to New Zealand's All Blacks earlier this month by defeating the U.S. men, 61-12, on Oct. 24 in Nashville. From rugby to American football A rugby ball is wider and heavier than an American football, with more rounded ends and no laces. A pass looks more like a two-handed heave than a traditional quarterback spiral. Points are scored similarly: by carrying the ball beyond the goal line or kicking between the posts. Tackling isn't very different in a scrum or at the line of scrimmage either. "The physicality is the big thing that transfers over," said Gray, a 6-foot-7, 318-pound lineman who is part of the NFL's International Player Pathway , which gives elite athletes from overseas an opportunity to develop football skills. "The footwork, though, is much more detailed in the NFL. Having good feet helped me transition over. Rugby league is a lot more fitness, a lot more endurance. 'Tackle, get up, make the next one.' American football is more based on power, strength, explosiveness. That's what I have to adapt to." item.title: Travis Kelce explains exactly why Seattle Seahawks are so hard to play against right now
item.description: Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Travis Kelce breaks down what Mike MacDonald has done with the Seattle Seahawks which makes them so difficult to beat. The Kansas City Chiefs were handed their first loss of the season in pretty spectacular fashion by the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday. The reigning Super Bowl champions won 20-3, completely shutting off Kenneth Walker III and Patrick Mahomes. It was no mean feat, as both have been in fine form to start the year. Travis Kelce has been looking like his old self for the most part, too. He wasn’t able to do much either, though. Kelce had four receptions in the game for 44 yards. He spoke about what makes the Seattle defence special. Travis Kelce breaks down Mike MacDonald’s defensive preference which makes Seattle tough The Seattle Seahawks have been the NFL’s best defence by total yards allowed this season, giving up just 233.9 yards per game. That’s No. 1 in the league. They’ve been excellent at limiting their opponents, with a sizeable gap between them and the second-ranked Minnesota Vikings. Kelce, in conversation with his brother Jason on their podcast, addressed how head coach Mike MacDonald is able to make that happen. “I feel like every time I face McDonald, he stays true to his style, and he has the personnel to be able to execute how he wants to,” the tight end said. “He’s going to kind of want to keep everything in front of him in terms of the back end of things. “But he’s always got an unbelievable D-line that just makes it tough to get to the second level on your double teams. It really forces you to be great on the backside of runs where, it’s typically the ball ends up coming back to that gap.” MacDonald became the first head coach in NFL history to win the Super Bowl while still being the primary defensive play-caller. The Seahawks are just 4-3 this season, but with their defense, one can never really write them off. item.description: Barcelona midfielder Fermin Lopez reflects on La Masia journey and life away from football Barcelona midfielder Fermin Lopez has reflected on the people and experiences that shaped his football journey, revealing how his first coach recognised his potential and why his parents have remained central to his success. In an interview with GQ (h/t SPORT ), the Spaniard also discussed his childhood in El Campillo, his move to La Masia and the simple routines that help him unwind away from football. His reflections come during a period in which Fermin is enjoying success both personally and professionally, following a difficult summer disrupted by an injury that ruled him out of representing Spain at the 2026 World Cup. Fermin recalls early signs of his footballing potential Fermin’s journey began in El Campillo, where his first coach , Rafael, quickly recognised that the youngster possessed qualities that could take him far in the game. “My first coach at El Campillo, from the moment he saw me, always told my parents that he saw something different in me. “His name is Rafael and I think he was the first person to coach me who saw something special in me, as well as the potential to go far in football,” he said. Football was already central to Fermin’s childhood, with much of his free time spent playing with friends. Fermin Lopez has looked back at his early career. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) His memories of those early years reflect a passion that extended well beyond organised training. “We used to play on the pitches; we’d sneak off to play, and I always had footballs in my room. The ball has always been my best friend, and football has been with me ever since.” Barcelona midfielder credits parents for his development Moving to La Masia at the age of 13 marked a major change in Fermin’s life, taking him away from the familiar surroundings of home. Throughout that transition and the challenges that followed, he identified his parents as his most dependable source of support. “Ever since I went to La Masia at the age of 13, I’d say my parents have been a cornerstone in my life and throughout my entire journey. “Whenever I’ve been feeling down, I’ve turned to them and they’ve supported and helped me. I’d say they’re two cornerstone figures who’ve always been there for me and have stood by me throughout this process.” Their encouragement has remained important throughout his development into a Barcelona first-team midfielder. item.description: Motorsport photo MotoGP points leader Marc Marquez claims to be wary of Jorge Martin's potential if his rival is passed fit to race at Sepang this weekend. Martin fractured his wrist in a heavy crash during the sprint race in Australia last weekend, falling 10 points behind Marquez in the championship. Factory Aprilia rider Martin has been declared fit to take part in Friday's opening session in Malaysia, but most expect him to be compromised if he races at all. Read Also: Jorge Martin braced for “really difficult, painful” MotoGP weekend with broken arm His Ducati counterpart Marquez said he wasn't buying that line. He referenced the stricter medical clearance threshold introduced since Marquez seriously compounded injuries by returning too soon after a crash at Jerez in 2020. "I feel and I believe that with the new protocols we have after my injury at Jerez, if they declare him fit, it means that he's able to ride," said the 33-year-old. "And if he's able to ride, he will be at a very high level because adrenaline is the best painkiller." Speaking in his native Spanish, Marquez went a step further in talking up his opponent: "I’m not just confident he’ll be fast on track, I'm certain of it. It won’t change how I approach my own work, but I’ll certainly be pushing to the maximum." Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team, Marc Marquez, Ducati Team Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team, Marc Marquez, Ducati Team The Spaniard also welcomed his countryman's efforts to race in Malaysia, saying it was better for the show. "Yeah, of course for the championship fight it's better that Jorge is there. I'm happy to see Martin on track." While Marquez offers soundbites designed not to tempt fate, it is worth pointing out that he landed what appeared to be a major psychological blow on Martin at Phillip Island. The 2024 world champion fell off during a close battle with Marquez , despite being the faster rider. That mental setback came on top of a not dissimilar mistake at the previous sprint in Indonesia, in which he was also quicker than Marquez. item.title: How Kimi Antonelli can win 2026 F1 title in Mexico City without even finishing race
item.description: Kimi Antonelli is on the cusp of becoming Formula 1 ’s youngest-ever world champion and looks set to claim the 2026 drivers’ title at the Mexican Grand Prix . The 20-year-old has made a mockery of the pre-season predictions which put his Mercedes teammate George Russell as the title favourite, with nine grand prix victories and 15 podiums in total. After his win in Austin, Antonelli currently has a 123-point lead over Russell with five rounds (and no sprint races) remaining this season, assuming F1 fulfils its end-of-season schedule with Qatar and Abu Dhabi. If those races can’t take place due to the conflict in the Middle East, a one-off round would conclude the campaign in Imola. Antonelli is also aiming to become the sport’s youngest world champion in its 76-year history. The current holder of this accolade is Sebastian Vettel, who won his first championship in 2010 at 23 years and 134 days. The Italian would also become only the third-ever driver – after Lewis Hamilton and Jacques Villeneuve – to win the championship in just his second season. Here’s how Antonelli can win the title this weekend in Mexico City - without even racing: Ninth or higher will guarantee the title Antonelli has a 123-point lead over second-placed Russell and a 124-point lead over Hamilton, with 125 points left on the table this season. After this round in Mexico City, there will be 100 points left to play for. As such, to win the title in Mexico City, Antonelli only needs to finish ninth or higher in Sunday’s race . Ninth would give him two points and while Russell could win the race and be 100 points behind, the Briton cannot catch the Italian’s race wins tally for the season, which is the tiebreaker if scores are level. However, even if Antonelli retires or finishes outside the top-10, he could still pick up the title. At a minimum, Russell or Hamilton need to win the grand prix to stretch the title race to Brazil next week. item.title: Manager reflects on draw with Dundee United
item.description: Manager reflects on draw with Dundee United After 11 Premiership games, and having played every other team once, Celtic find themselves four points clear at the top of the table. Martin O’Neill’s side are four points better off than at this stage last season and have won nine out of their 11 games in the campaign. Indeed, the only points dropped have been in two home games, and while Thursday night’s 2-2 draw with Dundee United saw the Champions maintain their Premiership lead, there was also a sense of frustration that it couldn’t have been extended. However, reflecting on the game, Martin O’Neill said that in a game his side should have won, over the course of the campaign it could still prove to be a valuable point gained, given the team had to come from behind. “It was a tough old game for us,” the Celtic manager told CelticPlayer . “I thought the second half performance was very strong and we had attack after attack. Yet, remarkably, they could have scored on a breakaway. “It was a big, big second half for us and we deserved the equaliser at least. And I just thought we were going to come up trumps towards the end. “The boys have given a lot in the game and they'll have to do the same again in a few days’ time. “We're going to be playing against Falkirk who are up for the game themselves. So it's just resting up, doing a little bit of work, but not that much because the games have been coming thick and fast.” CELTICPLAYER UNIQUE ANGLE Celtic drew 2-2 with Dundee United on Wednesday night to remain four points clear at the top of the table. item.description: INDIANAPOLIS -- The Philadelphia 76ers rode the roller coaster on Thursday in their road matchup with the Indiana Pacers . The Sixers led by 10 at halftime, but then got blitzed in the third quarter when the Pacers outscored them 36-13, but Philadelphia responded by outscoring Indiana 39-21 in the fourth to win it 114-109 on the road. Tyrese Maxey exploded in the fourth and then led Philadelphia with 27 points and five rebounds, Jaylen Brown added 20 points and 10 rebounds, Joel Embiid had 21 points and 11 rebounds, while LeBron James added 13 points, five rebounds, and 10 assists. Anfernee Simons had 20 points, and VJ Edgecombe added eight points and seven rebounds. Here are the three biggest takeaways for the Sixers after a win over the Pacers: Maxey's big fourth quarter The Sixers needed somebody out on the perimeter to do something on the offensive end in order to close this game out. Through three quarters, Maxey only had 10 points on 4-for-10 shooting. Then, the 2-time All-Star flipped the switch as he scored 17 points on 4-for-8 shooting and shot 7-for-8 from the foul line. He flipped the game on its head and he was the big reason why the Sixers were able to walk away with the win. The Pacers deserve credit for being physical with him and not allowing anything easy, but Maxey breaking out was a huge storyline in this win. "JB was on me beginning of the fourth quarter just about being aggressive and doing what I do," Maxey said after the win. "I think I just kind of let the game come to me. We've got a lot of different guys out here that can do a lot of different things. So it's going to be nights where shots are limited. That's just how the game flows and that's OK." item.title: ‘Drawing a blank’ – Robert Saleh seemingly forgets motivational speech for Titans in awkward clip
item.description: Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images Robert Saleh was speaking to reporters and describing what he said to the Tennessee Titans before he completely lost his train of thought. Saleh has been under the microscope ever since he took over as head coach of the Titans, following a second stint as the defensive coordinator for the San Francisco 49ers. The Titans have started the season 1-6 and have not looked great under Saleh. And his latest awkward moment during a press conference has only raised more questions about his fit as head coach. Robert Saleh loses his train of thought over Titans motivational talk during press conference Speaking to reporters ahead of the Tennessee Titans’ loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, HC Robert Saleh spoke about what he told the players as they continue to find their stride. While explaining his mindset to the reporters, Saleh began describing his message to the team, before immediately losing his train of thought. Saleh said: “We’ve just got to keep going through the process of learning how to finish. In the most extreme times, and this is what I told the team about today, and this is for all humans, not just football players. “In the most adverse moments, in the most pressure-packed moments, you’re always going to be… ummm… I’m drawing a blank. (to assistant coach) Do you remember what I said?” It was an awkward look for Saleh, who is already under pressure for not getting the most out of a young Titans team that many felt had a lot of potential coming into the new season. It doesn’t help that Saleh’s previous stint as head coach of the New York Jets ended disastrously, as management let him go for failing to get the best out of Aaron Rodgers and a strong offensive unit early into the 2024 season. item.description: New Episode of BBOC: Syracuse University Director of Athletics Bryan Blair On the latest episode of JohnWallStreet Presents: Big Business on Campus , a college sports podcast powered by Playfly Sports, JohnWallStreet Founder Corey Leff and Playfly Sports Chairman Michael Schreiber sit down with Syracuse University Director of Athletics Bryan Blair. It's activity. And you [increase activity levels] one, by increasing bodies, [and] two, [by keeping] a focus on the [outreach]. ...Then it turns into a math equation. I need to raise this much, so that means I need to ask this many times of this many people with this much capacity,” Blair said. “ It takes a little bit of expense to [grow]. Sometimes people don't want to hear that, and in college athletics, we sometimes try to cut our way to prosperity. You can't do that and make the jumps that we need to make. So [we’re going] to invest. [We’ve] got to be willing to take some risks and know that [we’ve] pre-given the right amount of rigor to [fundraising to] make those dreams come true.” Central New York’s Renaissance Creating a Premium Growth Opportunity for SU Premium seating remains one of Syracuse University’s largest untapped commercial opportunities. item.title: Former team-mate ready to put the final nail in Carrick’s United coffin: match storylines for landmark Chelsea encounter
item.description: Former team-mate ready to put the final nail in Carrick’s United coffin: match storylines for landmark Chelsea encounter Manchester United travel to West London to take on Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday lunchtime. The Red Devils have faced off against the Blues 199 times , meaning this match will be the 200th competitive game between the two rivals. United have come out on top 85 times in history, with Chelsea winning 57. There have also been 57 draws during the storied fixture. Here are three storylines to get the blood pumping. United closing in on unwanted record After Michael Carrick’s side lost 0-3 at home to AFC Bournemouth last Sunday, they had officially gone six Premier League matches without a win. This is already the second-longest winless streak in their Premier League history. The longest arrived in May 2025 when they went eight matches without a win. Nonetheless, with matches against Chelsea, Aston Villa and Liverpool to come, it is not exactly clear where the next win will come from. United are still some way off their worst ever run, not winning in 16 consecutive matches way back in the 1929-1930 season. Chelsea record Fortunately, the Red Devils have quite a respectable record as of late against Saturday’s opponents. In their last ten matches against the Blues, they have only lost twice. There have been four United wins, including two last season, and four draws since 2021. Former players Man United and Chelsea have had a lot of former players play for one another over the years. Andrey Santos has not had the best start to his United career, but he moved from Chelsea in the summer and, with Kobbie Mainoo still out, he will likely get another chance to start in the midfield against his former team. One player United will not want to face is their former player Danny Welbeck. The Carrington youth product moved to Stamford Bridge in the summer and has haunted United many times in the past, scoring six times against them for Brighton and Arsenal.

item.description: Iraola praises Liverpool teenager after man-of-the-match Chelsea performance Andoni Iraola praised the performance of Trey Nyoni after the Liverpool midfielder was named man of the match during the club’s Carabao Cup win over Chelsea. Liverpool reached the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup after beating Chelsea 6-5 on penalties at Anfield, following a 1-1 draw in normal time. Iraola opted to rotate his team for the clash, ahead of a Premier League meeting with Arsenal this weekend, and handed Nyoni a start in central midfield. The 19-year-old has been on the fringes of the first team this season and impressed, earning the Player of the Match award from Liverpool’s official social media channels. Iraola said Nyoni did ‘very well’ and was pleased how his youngsters handled the occasion, with academy graduate Lewis Koumas also starting against Chelsea. “I think he has done very well. Really well. It’s good for the young players especially to live these experiences in cup competitions, where if you lose you are out,” Iraola said in his post-match press conference. “We have been losing and then the draw. Then they haven’t been there in the penalty shootout but they lived the feelings. They played under pressure against a very good team. item.title: South Korea boss backs Son as captain after rift rumours
item.description: Son Heung-min has been called up by South Korea for friendlies next month against Saudi Arabia and Qatar (Philip FONG) Son Heung-min will continue as South Korea captain despite reports of friction between the former Tottenham striker and his senior international team-mates, coach Robert Moreno said Thursday. Moreno named Son, now 34 and playing for LAFC in Major League Soccer, in his squad for friendlies against Saudi Arabia and Qatar next month. He also selected experienced Europe-based trio Kim Min-jae, Hwang Hee-chan and Hwang In-beom, who reports say were ready to quit the national team last month. Moreno said he had held "many conversations with the players" since taking over on an interim basis after South Korea's World Cup flop in North America. "I spent more time communicating than training," the Spaniard said at a press conference that lasted more than an hour. "Even in the best teams people can have different opinions. What matters is how those differences are resolved." Moreno's contract is set to expire after the two friendlies, although South Korean football chiefs could keep him on for the Asian Cup, scheduled for Saudi Arabia in January. When asked about Son's leadership role in the team, Moreno said: "The captain is Son Heung-min. I have nothing more to say." Speculation about discord emerged after Bayern Munich defender Kim threw his boots in anger after being substituted in the second half of a 0-0 home friendly draw with Venezuela this month. Kim said afterwards that "every player needs to put their head down and give it their all", fuelling talk of divisions within the squad. Moreno said "the team is healthy" and backed the players to work together. "I believe you can find the answer in what I have said today and the squad that has been announced," he said. South Korea's football association this month told fans to stop "excessive personal attacks" on players. The national team is in the crosshairs after a poor showing at the World Cup, which saw coach Hong Myung-bo quit after they failed to get past the group stage. amk/pst

item.title: Bearman Has Scored 23 of Haas’s 30 Points. Now He Reportedly Wants $6.7 Million
item.description: Oliver Bearman has scored 23 of Haas’s 30 points in the 2026 Formula 1 season, and he reportedly wants to be paid like it: €6 million, about $6.7 million, a year to stay with the team. The figure comes from F1 business writer Marc Limacher, as Read Motorsport reported . Haas is reportedly unwilling to pay it, which has slowed talks on a 2027 deal, as we reported this week . Neither Bearman nor Haas has confirmed the number. What Bearman Is Paid Now RacingNews365’s estimates of 2026 base salaries put Bearman on about $1 million, among the lowest on the grid. Teams don’t publish contracts, and the estimates leave out bonuses and personal sponsorship, according to RacingNews365 . Here’s how that compares with points scored after 18 rounds: Driver Team Estimated 2026 salary 2026 points Max Verstappen Red Bull $70 million 236 Lewis Hamilton Ferrari $60 million 241 Esteban Ocon Haas $7 million 7 Isack Hadjar Red Bull $5 million 105 Kimi Antonelli Mercedes $2 million 365 Oliver Bearman Haas $1 million 23 Liam Lawson Racing Bulls $1 million 77 The raise Bearman is reportedly asking for would put him at about what his teammate is estimated to earn. Ocon, who leaves Haas after this season, has 7 points. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli has won nine Grands Prix on an estimated $2 million. Esteban Ocon and Oliver Bearman at the Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid on Sept. 12, 2026. (Photo by Simon Galloway/LAT Images) Why Bearman Says It’s Out of His Hands Haas has already confirmed Ferrari junior Rafael Cámara as Ocon’s replacement for 2027, but it hasn’t confirmed Bearman alongside him. Both sides say they want to keep going. “I think on our side as well, if I’m not mistaken, we’re very sure that we want to continue working together, and the only sticking points are kind of out of my hands, more contractual points,” Bearman told reporters at the US Grand Prix. He’s also a Ferrari junior, and he made it clear Haas isn’t where he plans to end up. “In terms of a midfield team, Haas is the team that I want to be with, and I see my future with,” he said. “But at some point, as well, I feel like I’ve earned the opportunity to go out and look for a top four team. And of course, with my link with Ferrari, that would be my ultimate goal.” For now, Ferrari has Charles Leclerc on a long-term deal and Lewis Hamilton in the other seat. Haas is seventh in the constructors’ standings with 30 points, and Bearman’s 23 points put him 13th in the drivers’ championship. The next race is the Mexico City Grand Prix on Sunday, Nov. 1, the next chance for either side to say where the talks stand.

item.title: Chelsea injury nightmare deepens as Xabi Alonso provides update on Maxence Lacroix blow against Liverpool
item.description: Liverpool v Chelsea - Carabao Cup Fourth Round - Getty Images Sport Chelsea’s injury problems have gone from bad to worse after Maxence Lacroix was forced to withdraw during their Carabao Cup showdown against Liverpool. The French defender appeared to suffer a hamstring issue during the first half at Anfield, adding further strain to Xabi Alonso’s already depleted squad. Lacroix limps off at Anfield The Blues crashed out of the Carabao Cup following a tense penalty shootout, with normal time ending 1-1 after Morgan Rogers and Cody Gakpo traded spot-kicks. However, the loss of their commanding centre-back will be of far greater concern to the Chelsea coaching staff. Lacroix pulled up while chasing Gakpo through midfield shortly after Liverpool's equaliser. He went down off the ball moments later and required treatment on the pitch before being replaced by Levi Colwill. The Frenchman walked slowly to the dressing room in clear distress, clutching the back of his left thigh while consulting with the club's medical trainers. Alonso reacts to fresh fitness setback Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso admitted the club will have to wait before discovering the full extent of the defender's muscle issue. Speaking after the final whistle, the Spaniard confirmed the medical team's initial suspicions. "Too early to tell. Probably he felt something on the hamstrings," Alonso said. "And we need a couple of days to check what's going to be the injury.” Mounting problems at Stamford Bridge Losing Lacroix represents a massive blow to Chelsea's defensive stability. The summer signing from Crystal Palace has been an ever-present figure this season, starting all eight Premier League fixtures and featuring in both Carabao Cup matches. His absence exacerbates an already severe selection crisis for Alonso. The west London outfit travelled north without Joao Pedro, Jamie Gittens, and Reece James due to injury, while talisman Cole Palmer missed the tie through suspension. Waiting game for the Blues Chelsea's medical staff will assess Lacroix over the coming days to determine a precise recovery timeline. A prolonged absence would stretch the squad to its limits, leaving Alonso heavily reliant on Colwill and his remaining defensive options during a busy autumn schedule. The manager must now regroup his depleted squad as they look to shake off their cup elimination and maintain momentum in the Premier League.

item.title: Real Madrid star misses group training due to overload; not a doubt for Racing Santander clash
item.description: Real Madrid star misses group training due to overload; not a doubt for Racing Santander clash Real Madrid’s impressive victory over Barcelona gave Jose Mourinho plenty of positives to build on in the coming weeks. One of the biggest positives to emerge for Los Blancos this season has been the growing influence of Arda Guler in midfield. The Turkish international played an important role in Sunday’s Clasico triumph, becoming one of Mourinho’s most trusted players. However, his absence from Wednesday’s group training session raised some concerns. According to journalist Alvaro Esteban , Guler worked indoors at Valdebebas due to muscular overload. The problem, however, is not considered serious enough to threaten his availability for Sunday’s La Liga encounter against Racing Santander. Arda Guler’s workload carefully managed after Clasico The 21-year-old completed an individual gym session rather than joining his teammates for the outdoor exercises. Captain Fede Valverde, who also experienced some discomfort against Barcelona , worked indoors, while Raul Asencio trained individually on the pitch. Guler’s individual training session is understood to have been a precaution, with the coaching staff managing his physical condition following an intense Clasico. Guler has emerged as an important star for Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Interestingly, Sunday’s encounter was the first time this season that the Turkish midfielder completed the full 90 minutes for Madrid. He produced an encouraging performance, creating problems for Barcelona’s defence and playing an important part in the move that led to Kylian Mbappe’s late winner. Mourinho has another important decision to make Guler’s growing importance has been one of the most positive developments under Mourinho this season. The midfielder has developed an excellent understanding with Mbappe, with his ability to receive between the lines and play forward passes giving Madrid another creative dimension. Mourinho needs to manage Guler’s minutes carefully. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The Portuguese manager has even tried him out as a defensive midfielder against Sevilla, showcasing the different ways he can be used. However, Mourinho now needs to manage Guler’s minutes. Los Blancos face a difficult schedule that involves a lot of travelling. Madrid face Racing Santander before travelling to Greece for their Champions League encounter against AEK Athens. Guler’s availability does not necessarily mean Mourinho needs to start him this weekend, with other options at his disposal. Keeping him fresh for important games is necessary for Madrid, and it remains to be seen what role he plays against Racing.

item.title: Eagles DC Vic Fangio takes all the blame for defense getting shredded by Cowboys on MNF
item.description: Eagles DC Vic Fangio takes all the blame for defense getting shredded by Cowboys on MNF appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Eagles ’ defense had no answers for the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football , and Vic Fangio is not pointing fingers at anyone but himself. Speaking to reporters days after Philadelphia’s 38-21 loss to Dallas at Lincoln Financial Field , the Eagles defensive coordinator owned the struggles of his unit. “I didn’t do a good enough job coaching,” Fangio said, via Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) It was a rough night for a defense that has been among the league’s most respected under Fangio, who helped lead the Eagles to a Super Bowl title in his first season with the team in 2024. The Cowboys ran all over Philadelphia, piling up 204 rushing yards on 38 carries. Javonte Williams did most of the damage with a career-high 155 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries, becoming Dallas’ first 150-yard rusher since Ezekiel Elliott in 2018. The Eagles also failed to record a single tackle for loss. Dak Prescott took advantage through the air as well. The Cowboys quarterback completed 15 of 27 passes for 212 yards and three touchdowns without an interception . CeeDee Lamb caught two of those scores, while George Pickens hauled in the other. The game was close for much of the night, featuring six lead changes. Philadelphia opened the second half with an 84-yard touchdown drive to go up 21-20, but Dallas answered with 18 unanswered points. Prescott’s third touchdown pass put the Cowboys back in front, Brandon Aubrey added a field goal, and Williams sealed it with a 2-yard touchdown run with 2:21 remaining after a DeMarvion Overshown interception. The Eagles were short-handed on both sides of the ball. Jalen Hurts, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks were all out, forcing Tanner McKee into the starting role, and Saquon Barkley left the game with a back injury . Even so, Fangio put the defense’s performance squarely on himself. His accountability comes at a difficult time for Philadelphia, which has now dropped five straight games to fall to 2-5 on the season. The Eagles will look to snap their skid and right the ship defensively when they host the NFC East-leading New York Giants next week. Fangio and his unit will need a much better showing to keep Philadelphia’s season from slipping away. item.description: PISCATAWAY – Rutgers football has beaten Michigan just one time, and if that’s going to change this weekend the Scarlet Knights need to play at a much higher level than they have this season. And that’s still the case even if the Wolverines have faced issues of their own – especially on offense, which has been subpar to say the least. Lonergan has already been ruled out against Michigan, according to the availability report that was released Oct. 28. How can Rutgers beat the Wolverines, or at the very least play a competitive game? Here are three keys that would help the Scarlet Knights do exactly that: 1. Avoid turning the ball over This continues to be a key because it’s an issue that has repeatedly hurt Rutgers this season. It’s especially true if either Surace or Ashenfelder, both relatively inexperienced quarterbacks, get the start. And it’s even more true against a stellar defense like the one Michigan has – the Wolverines are allowing just 250.1 yards per game (best in the Big Ten) and 15.7 points per game (seventh). item.title: Rogers admits penalty loss to Liverpool ‘worst way to lose a game’
item.description: Rogers admits penalty loss to Liverpool ‘worst way to lose a game’ Morgan Rogers has said Chelsea’s Carabao Cup exit on penalties is ‘probably the worst way to lose a game’. Chelsea lost to Liverpool in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup on Wednesday night after a shootout defeat at Anfield. Rogers had opened the scoring from the penalty spot for Chelsea, but Cody Gakpo’s equaliser, also from the spot, sent the tie into a shootout. A marathon shootout saw Liverpool prevail 6-5, and Rogers said Chelsea are gutted with the outcome. However, he said there was much to be positive about after a ‘really good performance’ away from home. “It is probably the worst way to lose a game,” said Rogers. “It was an even game and at times we had the better of it. In the first half we quietened down the crowd, had got our foot in the game and taken the lead. To concede so quickly was difficult. “I thought we started the second half really well, and we could have got in front a few times; we had a few chances towards the end. I’m a bit disappointed because I had some half-chances, half-moments that I’d have liked to have put away. They did as well. “It was a really good performance, really good game. Barcelona dressing room identifies reasons behind consecutive defeats as squad meeting lifts morale
item.description: Barcelona dressing room identifies reasons behind consecutive defeats as squad meeting lifts morale Barcelona suffered consecutive defeats against PSG and Real Madrid, which raised questions about Hansi Flick’s team’s performances. However, despite these setbacks, the players remain convinced that their problems can be corrected and that their ambitions for the season remain intact. According to journalist Jose Alvarez, speaking on El Chiringuito TV (h/t FCB World ), the atmosphere within Barcelona’s dressing room has improved considerably following Wednesday’s team barbecue. The team-bonding event was reportedly organised by the squad’s leaders , with Raphinha and Rodri spearheading the initiative. Barcelona players acknowledge mistakes behind recent defeats The gathering, attended by Flick, his coaching staff and the players, provided an opportunity to discuss football openly and encourage one another after a difficult week. Rather than attributing the defeats to external circumstances, the players acknowledged that their own mistakes had played a decisive role. Barcelona captain Raphinha helped organise a barbecue for the squad. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) They identified a lack of intensity, unusually careless passing, poor coverage of space and ineffective pressing as the main reasons behind the disappointing results. Importantly, the squad also reminded itself that Barcelona remain three points clear at the top of La Liga, despite losing Sunday’s Clasico. “Without those mistakes, we can win everything, because we have the best possible team,” was the message shared within the dressing room, according to Alvarez. The bigger picture still looks positive The main reason the past week feels so deflating from a Barcelona perspective is how high they were flying before it. This was not a team under Hansi Flick that was scraping over the line in games. They were scoring goals against opponents for fun. Supporters took the victories for granted, and the losses against PSG and Real Madrid have brought them back to earth. Two games should not make everyone forget Barcelona’s start to the season. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) No team wins titles by winning every single game they play, and these two losses cannot overshadow Barcelona’s brilliant start to the season. The important thing to remember is that the Catalans are still in full control of the situation in La Liga and the Champions League. They face Aston Villa and Atletico Madrid in the next three games, two big clashes that give Flick’s men a chance to respond. It remains to be seen whether these two defeats are a minor aberration in Barcelona’s season and whether the team can bounce back in style against Alaves this weekend.
